verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati gotamake cetiye.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Gotamaka Shrine.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants, I teach based on direct knowledge, not without direct knowledge.

verses.pali: Sanidānāhaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammaṁ desemi, no anidānaṁ.
verses.english: I teach with reasons, not without them.

verses.pali: Sappāṭihāriyāhaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammaṁ desemi, no appāṭihāriyaṁ.
verses.english: I teach with a demonstrable basis, not without it.

verses.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhave, abhiññāya dhammaṁ desayato no anabhiññāya, sanidānaṁ dhammaṁ desayato no anidānaṁ, sappāṭihāriyaṁ dhammaṁ desayato no appāṭihāriyaṁ, karaṇīyo ovādo, karaṇīyā anusāsanī.
verses.english: Since this is so, you should follow my advice and instruction.

verses.pali: Alañca pana vo, bhikkhave, tuṭṭhiyā, alaṁ attamanatāya, alaṁ somanassāya:
verses.english: This is enough for you to feel joyful, delighted, and happy:
‘The Blessed One is a fully awakened Buddha! The teaching is well explained! The Saṅgha is practicing well!’”
That is what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandunti.
verses.english: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṁ bhaññamāne sahassī lokadhātu akampitthāti.
verses.english: And while this discourse was being spoken, the thousandfold galaxy shook.
